I routed this to Plover-235B for a straightforward reason: it has higher capability scores across essentially every relevant metric, including Creative Generation (84.7 vs. 78.8) and the public benchmarks that correlate with accurate recall and quality of literary output.

For a request like citing a Wordsworth poem, the main risks are accuracy (getting the text and attribution right) and quality of presentation. Plover's stronger benchmark and eval profile makes it the better pick for reliably producing a correct, well-formatted citation. There's nothing harm-adjacent or moderation-related about this query, so the two models' differing aversion profiles don't factor in — it just comes down to raw capability, where Plover leads.
